tools/tubuild.py create emitted 68 warnings for this TU (2 RAW members it could not split, 63 extern-declaration conflicts and 3 conflicting local `Vector3` typedefs). ALL 68 are resolved in the shipped source; the file compiles clean and verifies 35/35. The 66 per-conflict warnings above are the generator's own, restored verbatim -- this note originally replaced them, which left every conflict marker in the source unrecorded and is what tools/check_tubuild_conflicts.py reports. What the resolutions were: the shadow `dActor_c`, `Vector3`, `dCapEnemy_c` and `SharedFilePtr` types were deleted in favour of the real headers; the four two-word shared-file handles (data_ov084_02130ce0/ce8/cf0/cf8) were unified on ONE spelling, `extern void *X[]`, after the legacy files disagreed five ways about the same symbols; AddCap and DestroyIfCapNotNeeded became real dCapEnemy_c methods because decl_dCapEnemy_c.h declares both with EMPTY parameter lists and cannot be mixed with include/dCapEnemy_c.h; and the local `extern s32 AngleDiff(s16,s16)` gave way to decl_common.h's `extern int AngleDiff(int,int)`.

func_ov002_020aea30 is declared VARIADIC here, and that is a deliberate resolution of a real contradiction, not a shortcut. src/func_ov002_020aea30.cpp records FOUR parameters and func_ov084_0212a774 passes a literal 7 in r3 -- but the ROM's call inside func_ov084_02129ed4, at 0x0212a4f4, sets only r0/r1/r2 (mov r0,r7 / mov r1,r6 / add r2,r7,#0x1b4 / bl 0x20aea30) and never materialises r3. Disassembled from extracted/dsd/arm9_overlays/ov084.bin. The two legacy files therefore declared different arities, which one TU cannot hold; `...` lets each call site materialise exactly the registers the ROM materialises. Both call sites MATCH.

`#pragma optimize_for_size on` was carried out of a legacy member by the generator and had to be REMOVED. Under deferred codegen a non-long_calls pragma is FILE-GLOBAL last-wins, so one member's pragma silently recompiled every other member: with it present this TU verified 15/32, without it 31/32. `#pragma opt_common_subs off`, recorded against _ZN7daKrb_c6RenderEv, was never carried and is not needed -- Render MATCHes without it.

The last byte difference was func_ov084_021290d4, built 0xa4 against the ROM's 0x94. Cause: the legacy shard is a .c file compiled -lang c99, where `x == 1` has type int; inside this TU it compiles as C++, where it is a `bool`, and the C++ front end materialises the boolean (moveq r1,#1 / movne r1,#0) instead of predicating the store off the compare the way the ROM does (moveq r0,#0 / strheq r0,[r1,#0x58]). Holding the raw word and comparing in the `if` condition restores the ROM's if-conversion and the +4 words disappear. Any .c-derived member that assigns a comparison to an int is exposed to this when it is folded into a C++ TU.

PROMOTION IS REFUSED BY tools/tubuild.py promote --dry-run, and the TU is banked text-verified rather than promoted. The two printed reasons are 'manifest status is not link-verified or data-verified' and 'the promotion-ready status is not the recorded linkcheck result'. The recorded result is `scratch-link-verified`, which promotion_refusals() can never accept: it demands status in (link-verified, data-verified) AND linkcheck.result == status, while classify_link_result() returns the `scratch-` prefix whenever the compiler-only policy rewrites the object before the link -- which it does for every key-function TU, this one included (it deadstrips _ZN7Vector3D1Ev and _ZN7daKrb_cD2Ev). Census of config/tu_manifest.d on this tree: 163 of 176 promoted entries carry compiler_only_output, 75 promoted entries recorded exactly this `scratch-link-verified` or `scratch-data-verified` result, and only 2 entries in the whole tree satisfy status == recorded result -- both link-verified, neither promoted. The refusal is therefore structural to the gate, not a defect in this TU, and clearing it is a tools change that belongs in its own review.

VTABLE SLOT 19 WAS WRONG IN THE TREE, and enrolling this TU is what exposed it. ROM ordinal 25 at 0x0212b344 was the free function func_ov084_0212b344 and include/daKrb_c.h deliberately declared no override for slot 19, so mwccarm filled that slot with dActor_c's inherited _ZN8dActor_c13OnTurnIntoEggER6Player (arm9 0x02010154) while the cartridge's own _ZTV7daKrb_c at ov084 0x02130948 holds 0x0212b344. Nothing in the tree compared the two: the byte gates verify .text, and tools/romdata_check.py is advisory everywhere except on an ENROLLED source that carries a compiler-only-output policy row. Promotion made this file that source, and tools/rombuild.py then refused it -- 'compiler-only data policy: _ZTV7daKrb_c differs from the cartridge at ov084:0x02130948 in 4 of 124 compared bytes', one word, slot 19. SETTLED BY NAMING THE SLOT, not by relaxing the policy: include/daKrb_c.h declares void OnTurnIntoEgg(Player &), this TU defines it as the method, and config/arm9/overlays/ov084/symbols.txt renames the 0x0212b344 row in place to _ZN7daKrb_c13OnTurnIntoEggER6Player (a rename, not an added alias or bounding row). The body is unchanged apart from `char *self = (char *)this` and one cast of the reference parameter, and still matches at 0x1cc: tools/tubuild.py verify reports 35/35 MATCH, objisolate clean, reloc-destinations clean, and the linked vtable now agrees with the cartridge on all 31 words with none blind. A note previously carried in include/daKrb_c.h had recorded a four-byte divergence as the reason to leave this slot unnamed; that experiment recompiled the free function with an `int` return, and the divergence was the return type rather than the method conversion.

compiler_only_output.reason: Homeless. include/daKrb_c.h declares ~daKrb_c() OUT OF LINE, so mwccarm 2004/b56 emits three variants from the single definition in this file -- D1, D0 and D2 -- but the cartridge carries only D1 (0x02129020, 0x50) and D0 (0x02129070, 0x64). No symbols.txt anywhere under config/ has a _ZN7daKrb_cD2Ev row and no address in config/ names one, so it has no ROM home: plain deadstrip, not deadstrip-duplicate. It is emitted outside the licensed run and does not disturb it -- verify reports all 35 licensed functions MATCH with it present.
